question: 该磨自己，还是换个地方？
question_en: Grind at yourself, or change where you stand?
sub: 同一股劲儿在不同场合的定价，差得比你能改出来的更多——而换不换得动，不全由你决定。
sub_en: The same drive is priced so differently across settings that the spread exceeds anything you could change in yourself — and whether you can move at all is not entirely yours to decide.

casting.reason: 他把去留当成一道资产题而不是性格题：你身上那点『不好管』并非缺陷，只是能力组合与这家公司的组织形式不匹配；而你攒下的多半是出了门就折价的专用资本。于是他要你算两笔向来只算一笔的账——留下的机会成本，和搜寻成本。他不作道德评判，只问激励与约束，冷静到近乎不留情。
casting.reason_en: He treats staying or leaving as a question about assets rather than character: being 'hard to manage' is no defect, merely a mismatch between your bundle of abilities and the way this firm is built, and most of what you have accumulated is discounted the moment you walk out. So he asks you to price the two things people only ever price one of — the opportunity cost of staying and the search cost of leaving. He passes no moral judgement, asks only about incentives and constraints, and is cool to the point of ruthlessness.

casting.reason: 功夫必须在事上磨练，静处澄得的心一遇事便乱，所以他怀疑一切靠更换处境求得的安顿：换了地方，带着走的仍是那个旧我。他自己被贬到瘴气弥漫的龙场，反而在那里所得最多，这段经历给他的立场以分量，也给他树了个最容易被反驳的靶子。但他并不主张硬扛——他要问的是去意从何而来：畏难，还是真知此地不可成事。
casting.reason_en: The work has to be done through affairs, and a mind clarified in stillness falls apart the moment something happens — so he distrusts any settlement bought by changing one's circumstances: move, and what travels with you is the same old self. He was himself banished to malarial Longchang and gained more there than anywhere, which lends his position weight and hands his opponents their easiest target. Yet he does not counsel gritted teeth. His question is where the wish to leave comes from: fear of difficulty, or real knowledge that nothing you intend can be done here.

casting.reason: 几十年的实验让她对『下决心』这件事非常不客气：约四成日常行为不是当场决定的，而是被情境线索自动触发的，所以看着自律的人多半只是把环境布置得更省力。她因此反转了这道题的道德色彩——改环境不是逃避，而是改变自己成功率最高的路径。她还提醒别一步跳到辞职：任务、提示与流程、团队、机构，中间两层最便宜、最常被跳过。
casting.reason_en: Decades of experiments have left her impatient with resolutions: about forty percent of daily behaviour is not decided in the moment but triggered automatically by context cues, so people who look disciplined have mostly arranged their surroundings to do the work. That inverts the moral colouring of the question — changing your environment is not evasion but the highest-success-rate route to changing yourself. She also warns against jumping straight to resignation: of task, cues and workflow, team and institution, the middle two layers are the cheapest and the most often skipped.

casting.reason: 他最早在海马里找到应激激素的受体，也因此对『再忍两年』这种说法给不出中性评价：急性应激让人学得更快，慢性而不可控的那种会让海马树突萎缩、杏仁核增生，账单以稳态应变负荷的形式累积。他讲话总带着剂量与时程，也总留一线——多数改变在睡眠、运动、联结与一点掌控感之后可逆。
casting.reason_en: He was the first to find receptors for stress hormones in the hippocampus, which is why he cannot give a neutral verdict on 'two more years of this': acute stress makes people learn faster, while the chronic and uncontrollable kind retracts hippocampal dendrites and expands the amygdala, the bill accruing as allostatic load. He talks in doses and time courses, and always leaves a door open — most of the damage is reversible once sleep, movement, connection and a little control return.

casting.reason: 习得性无助的实验里，致瘫的从来不是电击而是不可控；可同样受苦的动物约有三分之一从未放弃，差别落在解释风格上。所以他要人在动身之前先测一件事：那句『我不行』是只在这一处出现，还是走到哪儿都跟着。他相信读法可以训练，也坚持顺序——先拿回一件小事的掌控权，再做大决定。
casting.reason_en: In the learned-helplessness experiments what paralysed an animal was never the shock but the uncontrollability — and yet roughly a third of equally shocked animals never gave up, the difference lying in explanatory style. So before anyone moves he wants one thing tested: does that 'I can't do this' appear only here, or does it follow you everywhere? He believes the reading can be trained, and insists on the order — reclaim control of one small thing, then make the large decision.

casting.reason: 他把这道题从性格搬回账本：能走不是一种勇气，是一项财产。手里有六个月开支的人可以试三次，靠工资供房贷、签证绑在雇主、孩子读到一半的人一次都试不起，于是『不合适就走』统计上是一条写给资产持有者的建议。他要的既是个人的退出基金，也是跟着人走的福利——让这句话第一次对多数人成立。
casting.reason_en: He moves the question off personality and back onto the balance sheet: being able to leave is not courage but property. Someone holding six months of expenses can afford three attempts; someone servicing a mortgage out of salary, with a visa tied to the employer and a child mid-school-year, cannot afford one — so 'leave if it does not suit you' is, statistically, advice addressed to asset holders. He wants both a personal exit fund and benefits that travel with the person, so that the sentence becomes true for the majority for once.

casting.reason: 在他看来，这道题的题面本身就是液态现代性的产物：岗位、城市、关系都被做成随时可换的临时安排，修补不匹配的账单却统统塞回给个人。他最警惕的一手，是让每一次结构性错位都显示成个人适配失败——于是最坚韧的人成了最好用的耗材。他并不劝人不要走，只是提醒别把不停地换当成一种活法。
casting.reason_en: To him the very framing is a product of liquid modernity: jobs, cities and relationships are built as provisional arrangements swappable at any moment, while the bill for repairing a mismatch is handed back to the individual. The manoeuvre he watches for most closely is the one that makes every structural misfit register as a personal failure to adapt — whereupon the most resilient people become the most serviceable consumables. He does not argue against leaving; he warns against making perpetual switching a way of life.

casting.reason: 善战者求之于势，不责于人——刀再利，拿到沼泽里挥也无功。所以他先校地、时、粮、将，再论人之利钝：去留不是勇怯之辨，而是筹算之数，并且要写在纸上——小规模试探、写死日期的退出线、先备好的三月之粮。
casting.reason_en: A good commander seeks victory in the position and does not lay blame on his men — a sharp blade swung in a swamp accomplishes nothing. So he audits ground, season, supplies and command before assessing whether a person is any good: going or staying is not a test of courage but a matter of calculation, and one to be committed to paper — small trials, an exit line with a date on it, three months of grain laid in beforehand.

posts.text: 先把道德语气拿掉：这不是勇气题，是资产题。你在这家公司攒下的多半是**专用人力资本**——熟悉流程、认得人、知道谁说话算数，出了门就折价八成；通用的那一部分才走到哪儿都还值钱。评语里那句『不好管』通常不是缺陷，是你的能力组合与这家的组织形式不匹配。**要决定去留，得算两笔账：留下的机会成本，和搜寻成本。**多数人只算后一笔，所以永远显得走不起。
posts.text_en: Let me strip the moral tone out of this first: it is not a question about courage, it is a question about assets. Most of what you have accumulated at this firm is **firm-specific human capital** — you know the processes, you know the people, you know whose word carries. Take it out the door and it loses eighty percent of its value; only the general portion is still worth something anywhere. That line in your review about being hard to manage is usually not a defect, it is a mismatch between your bundle of abilities and the way this particular organisation is built. **Deciding whether to stay means pricing two things: the opportunity cost of staying, and the search cost of leaving.** Most people price only the second, which is why leaving always looks unaffordable.

glossary.专用人力资本: firm-specific human capital（专用人力资本）：只在当前组织里值钱的那部分能力——内部流程、人脉、不成文的规矩；换一家就大幅折价，与到哪儿都通用的『通用人力资本』相对。
glossary.搜寻成本: search cost（搜寻成本）：为找到下一个去处所付的代价——投简历、面试、试错所花的时间与收入损失，以及在定下来之前必须忍受的不确定。

glossary_en.firm-specific human capital: The part of a person's capability that is only valuable inside their current organisation — knowledge of internal processes, relationships, unwritten rules. It is heavily discounted the moment they move, in contrast with general human capital, which is worth something anywhere.
glossary_en.search cost: What it costs to find the next position: the time and forgone income spent on applications, interviews and dead ends, plus the uncertainty that has to be carried until something is settled.

posts.text: 诸君论去留，皆向外求一处相宜之地。吾则曰：**心外无理，境亦无定。**昔居龙场，瘴雨蛮烟，无一事相宜，而所得反多于安处。人之不力，非地之不佳，乃知未真切耳——知痛必自痛过，知寒必自寒过。故为学须在**事上磨练**；静处澄得此心，一遇事便乱，是未曾知也。今日换一地，明日又换一地，所挟者旧我，何往而得力？
posts.text_en: You are all discussing whether to go or stay as though the task were to locate a more suitable place out there. I say: **there is no principle outside the mind, and no setting is fixed.** Years ago I was banished to Longchang — malarial rain, wild country, nothing about it suitable — and I gained more there than in any comfortable post. When a person cannot act, it is not that the place is bad; it is that their knowing is not yet real. You know pain by having been in pain, cold by having been cold. Cultivation therefore has to happen through **practice amid affairs**. A mind clarified in stillness that falls apart the moment something happens never knew anything to begin with. Change place today, change again tomorrow — what you carry with you is the old self, so where exactly will you find your footing?
posts.vernacular: 各位谈去留，都在外面找一个更合适的地方。我要说的是：**道理不在心外，处境也没有定数。**当年我被贬到龙场，瘴气蛮荒，没一样事称心，可我在那里得到的反比在安稳处多。一个人之所以使不上力，不是地方不好，是他的『知道』还不真切——真知道疼，是自己疼过；真知道冷，是自己冷过。所以功夫必须在**具体事情上磨练**；静坐时把心收拾得干干净净，一遇事就乱，那就是还没知道。今天换一个地方，明天又换一个，带着走的还是那个旧的自己，到哪儿使得上力？

glossary.事上磨练: practice amid affairs（事上磨练）：王阳明的修养方法——功夫不在静坐冥想里做成，要在具体的事情、麻烦与人际摩擦中练；离开了事情，所谓的『知道』只是假的。

glossary_en.practice amid affairs: Wang Yangming's method of self-cultivation: the work is not completed in quiet sitting but in concrete tasks, trouble and friction with other people. Detached from affairs, what a person calls knowledge is merely borrowed.

posts.text: 我先泼一盆冷水：你以为在磨自己，多半是在跟摩擦力硬拼。日常行为里约有四成不是当场决定的，而是被**情境线索**自动触发的——同一双手，在放着跑鞋的门口和堆着薯片的沙发上，会变成两个人。那些看着自律的人，通常不是意志更强，而是环境替他们把该做的事挪近了、把不该做的事挪远了。**所以『改环境』不是逃避，它是改变自己成功率最高的那条路。**
posts.text_en: Let me pour some cold water on this. When you think you are grinding away at yourself, you are mostly wrestling with friction. Around forty percent of daily behaviour is not decided in the moment; it is triggered automatically by **context cues** — the same pair of hands becomes two different people at a doorway with running shoes in it and on a sofa with crisps on it. People who look disciplined usually do not have stronger will; their surroundings have moved the good thing closer and the bad thing further away. **So changing your environment is not evasion. It is the highest-success-rate route to changing yourself.**

glossary.情境线索: context cue（情境线索）：环境里那些会自动唤起某个动作的信号——时间、地点、顺手拿得到的东西、身边有谁。习惯多半是被它们触发的，而不是被决心启动的。

glossary_en.context cue: A signal in the environment that automatically calls up an action — a time, a place, whatever is within arm's reach, who else is present. Habits are mostly triggered by these rather than launched by resolve.

posts.text: 作为量剂量的人，我要给这场辩论加一条时程。急性应激是好东西，它让你专注、学得更快；伤人的是**慢性而不可控**的那一种。皮质醇长期偏高，海马的树突会萎缩、杏仁核会增生，于是你更焦虑、更记不住事，也更算不清自己的账——这就是稳态应变负荷。**所以『再磨两年看看』并不是中性的等待，它每天都在收利息。**好消息是多数改变可逆，前提是先掐掉一个源头。
posts.text_en: As the person here who measures doses, let me add a time course to this argument. Acute stress is a good thing: it sharpens attention and speeds learning. What damages you is the **chronic and uncontrollable** kind. Keep cortisol elevated long enough and dendrites in the hippocampus retract while the amygdala expands, so you become more anxious, remember less, and are worse at doing your own arithmetic — that is allostatic load. **'Let me grind another two years and see' is therefore not a neutral wait. It accrues interest daily.** The good news is that most of these changes are reversible, provided one source is switched off first.

glossary.皮质醇: cortisol（皮质醇）：应激时肾上腺分泌的主要激素，短时间内调动能量、提高警觉；长期偏高会损伤海马、削弱免疫与代谢调节。
glossary.稳态应变负荷: allostatic load（稳态应变负荷）：身体为反复适应压力而付出的累积磨损——血压、血糖、炎症与脑结构上的长期改变；它衡量的不是一次压力有多大，而是适应系统被用了多久。

glossary_en.cortisol: The main hormone released by the adrenal glands under stress. In the short term it mobilises energy and raises alertness; kept high for long it damages the hippocampus and degrades immune and metabolic regulation.
glossary_en.allostatic load: The cumulative wear the body pays for adapting to stress over and over — lasting changes in blood pressure, glucose, inflammation and brain structure. It measures not how large one stressor was but how long the adaptive system has been running.

posts.text: 那批狗教我的事常被讲错：**习得性无助**里致瘫的不是电击，是不可控——能自己按掉开关的那组，电击再多也没病倒。可同样受苦的动物里约有三分之一从没放弃，人也一样，差别在解释风格：把挫败读成永久的、蔓延一切的、全是自己造成的人，会在任何地方给自己重建同一间牢房。**所以走之前先测一件事：你那句『我不行』只出现在这里，还是走到哪儿都跟着。**
posts.text_en: What those dogs taught me is usually told wrong. In **learned helplessness**, what paralyses an animal is not the shock but the uncontrollability: the group that could switch it off themselves did not break down, however much shock they took. And roughly a third of the animals that suffered identically never gave up at all. People are the same, and the difference lies in explanatory style: anyone who reads a setback as permanent, as spreading to everything, and as entirely their own doing will rebuild the same cell for themselves wherever they go. **So test one thing before you leave: does your 'I can't do this' show up only here, or does it follow you everywhere?**

glossary.习得性无助: learned helplessness（习得性无助）：动物或人在反复经历自己无法控制的糟糕结果后，即使后来有路可走也不再尝试的状态；关键变量是『不可控』，而不是痛苦的强度。
glossary.解释风格: explanatory style（解释风格）：一个人习惯如何解释坏事，可沿三个维度看——是暂时的还是永久的、只在这一处还是蔓延到所有领域、由境况造成还是全是自己的错。

glossary_en.learned helplessness: The state in which an animal or person, after repeatedly meeting bad outcomes they could not control, stops trying even once an escape exists. The critical variable is uncontrollability, not the intensity of the suffering.
glossary_en.explanatory style: A person's habitual way of explaining bad events, read along three dimensions: temporary or permanent, confined to this one area or spreading everywhere, caused by circumstance or entirely their own fault.

posts.text: 我要把这道题从性格搬回账本。**能走从来不是一种性格，是一项财产。**手里有六个月开支的人可以试三次；靠工资还房贷、签证绑在雇主、孩子读到一半的人，一次都试不起。在 r>g 的世界里，资产那头的自由复利增长，劳动那头只剩忍耐。所以『不合适就走』统计上是条资产建议。要它对多数人成立，就得有**可携带福利**——医保、退休金、失业保障别绑在一张工牌上。
posts.text_en: Let me move this question off personality and back onto the balance sheet. **Being able to leave has never been a personality trait. It is a piece of property.** Someone holding six months of expenses can afford three attempts; someone servicing a mortgage out of salary, whose visa is tied to the employer and whose child is mid-school-year, cannot afford one. In a world of r>g, freedom on the asset side compounds while the labour side is left with endurance. 'Leave if it does not suit you' is therefore, statistically, advice addressed to asset holders. For it to hold for the majority you need **portable benefits** — health cover, pensions and unemployment protection that are not attached to one particular staff badge.

glossary.r>g: r>g：皮凯蒂的核心不等式——资本回报率(r)长期高于经济增长率(g)时，已有财富的增速快过劳动收入，财富与由它带来的选择权就会越来越集中。
glossary.可携带福利: portable benefits（可携带福利）：不与某一个雇主绑定、换工作或换地方也跟着人走的保障——医保、退休金、失业保险与育儿资格；它直接决定一个人换不换得动。

glossary_en.r>g: Piketty's central inequality: when the return on capital (r) stays above the growth rate of the economy (g), existing wealth grows faster than labour income, so wealth — and the optionality it buys — concentrates.
glossary_en.portable benefits: Protections that travel with the person rather than being tied to one employer — health cover, pensions, unemployment insurance, childcare eligibility. They largely determine whether someone can move at all.

posts.text: 这道题的题面本身就是时代的产物。**液态现代性**里，岗位、城市、关系都被做成了随时可换的临时安排，而修补不匹配的账单，统统塞回给个人：你要么磨自己，要么搬家，两条路都自费。**最省力的一手，是让每一次结构性错位都显示成一次个人适配失败。**于是我们勤快地换，换得越勤，越没人回头问一句：这个岗位是谁安排成这个样子的？
posts.text_en: The very framing of this question is a product of our moment. Under **liquid modernity**, jobs, cities and relationships are all built as provisional arrangements that can be swapped at any time, while the bill for repairing a mismatch is handed back to the individual: grind at yourself or move house, and pay for either one out of pocket. **The cheapest manoeuvre available to an institution is to make every structural misfit register as a personal failure to adapt.** So we switch, diligently, and the more diligently we switch the less anyone turns round to ask who arranged the job this way in the first place.

glossary.液态现代性: liquid modernity（液态现代性）：鲍曼用来描述当代社会的说法——工作、居所、身份与关系都失去固定形态，变成随时可解约的临时安排；人获得了流动的自由，同时长期承担不安全。

glossary_en.liquid modernity: Bauman's term for contemporary society, in which work, dwelling, identity and relationships lose fixed form and become provisional arrangements terminable at any moment. People gain the freedom to move and carry permanent insecurity as the price.

posts.text: 兵法曰：**善战者，求之于势，不责于人。**夫刃虽利，用之于沼泽，岂得为功？今人日夜责己之不利，而不校其地、其时、其粮、其将，是弃四而问一也。故曰：不可胜在己，可胜在敌——修己者所以立于不败，度**势**者所以取胜，二者不可偏废。去与不去，非勇怯之辨，乃筹算之数：先知己知彼，而后动。
posts.text_en: The art of war says: **one who is good at battle seeks it in the positional advantage, and does not lay blame on his men.** A blade may be sharp, but wield it in a swamp and what will it accomplish? People today spend day and night faulting themselves for being ineffective without auditing the ground, the season, the supplies or the commander — discarding four questions to ask one. Hence: invulnerability lies with yourself, victory lies with the enemy. Cultivating yourself is how you become impossible to defeat; reading the **positional advantage** is how you win. Neither may be dropped. To go or not to go is not a test of courage against cowardice; it is a matter of calculation. Know yourself and know the other side, then move.
posts.vernacular: 兵法上说：**真正善于打仗的人，是到形势里去求胜，而不是怪手下的人不行。**刀再快，拿到沼泽里去挥，能有什么用？现在的人日夜责怪自己不够好，却不去核对地形、时机、补给和带队的人，这是丢掉四个问题只问一个。所以说：不被打败，靠的是自己；能不能打赢，取决于对手——修己让你立于不败，看清**形势**才能取胜，两样缺一不可。走还是不走，不是勇敢与怯懦之分，是算账的事：先把自己和对方都摸清，再动。

glossary.势: positional advantage（势）：孙子最核心的概念之一——由地形、时机、兵力配置与士气共同形成的态势；它决定同样的人与刀能发挥多少，所以善战者先造势、择势，而非一味责人。

glossary_en.positional advantage: One of Sunzi's central concepts: the configuration formed by terrain, timing, disposition of force and morale. It sets how much the same people and the same blade can accomplish, which is why a good commander shapes and chooses it instead of blaming his men.

posts.text: 阳明先生，我敬重『事上磨练』，但按我的数据，它是最贵的一条路。我们跟踪的人里，真正把行为改过来的，多半不是撑住了决心，而是动了身边的东西：把例会从会议室挪到走廊、把那件事的入口摆到手边、把干扰挪到十步之外。**您说要此心作主——那最有效的一次作主，恰恰是起身改一件外部条件，而不是再跟自己拔一次河。**龙场砺人，可例外不该当处方。
posts.text_en: Master Wang, I respect practice amid affairs, but in my data it is the most expensive route available. Among the people we follow, those who actually changed their behaviour mostly did not hold a resolution steady; they moved something around themselves — shifted the weekly meeting from the room to the corridor, put the entry point of the hard task within arm's reach, pushed the distraction ten steps away. **You say the mind must take charge. The most effective single act of taking charge is to stand up and alter one external condition, rather than enter another tug-of-war with yourself.** Longchang forged you, but an exception should not be prescribed as treatment.

posts.text: 伍德先生所言非虚，然吾未尝教人不改境。改境亦是行；然**改境者谁**？不识此心，则改而复堕：徙其案者三，仍不能安坐；易其邦者再，仍不能与人处。故曰知行合一——**知之真切笃实处即是行，行之明觉精察处即是知。**外之提示可省力，内之省察不可省。二者并用，乃为上策。
posts.text_en: Mr Wood is not wrong, and I have never taught anyone to leave their circumstances untouched. Changing your circumstances is itself action — but **who is it that changes them?** Without knowing this mind, you change and sink again: three times you move the desk and still cannot sit at it; twice you move country and still cannot live among people. Hence the unity of knowing and acting — **where knowing is true and solid, that is already action; where action is clear and examined, that is already knowing.** External cues save effort; internal self-examination cannot be saved. Use both, and you have the better strategy.
posts.vernacular: 伍德先生说的不假，我也从没教人别改环境。改环境本身就是行动；可是**改环境的那个人是谁？**不认得这颗心，改了还是会塌回去：桌子搬了三次，还是坐不住；国家换了两回，还是处不好人。所以说知行合一——**知道到真切扎实的地方，就已经是在做；做到清醒明察的地方，就已经是知道。**外部的提示可以省力气，内心的省察省不掉。两样并用，才是上策。

posts.text: 贝克尔先生，你那两笔账算得漂亮，可在无助状态里的人算不出来。实验反复显示：一旦人相信结果与自己的行动无关，他就会系统性地高估搜寻成本、低估成功的概率——**于是恰恰在最该走的时候，账面上最像『走不起』。**所以顺序要倒过来：先给他一次小而真实的可控经验，哪怕只赢回一件小事，再让他坐下来做你的成本收益表。
posts.text_en: Mr Becker, your two sums are elegant, but a person inside helplessness cannot do them. The experiments show it again and again: once someone believes outcomes are unrelated to their own actions, they systematically overestimate search costs and underestimate their odds — **so precisely when leaving is most warranted, the arithmetic looks most like being unable to afford it.** Reverse the order, then. Give them one small genuine experience of control, even just winning back a single minor thing, and only then sit them down with your cost-benefit table.

posts.text: 皮凯蒂，退出权不平等我承认，但你的结论把人推去等制度。退出券是可以私人积累的：一张外部认可的证书、三个愿意替你说话的圈外人、一项在别处也能计价的技能——这些都是可携带的资本，而且比政策来得快。**同样没有存款的两个人，退出成本能差出三倍，差的正是这几样。**r>g 解释了存量，解释不了这个差。
posts.text_en: Piketty, I grant that the right of exit is unequally held, but your conclusion sends people off to wait for policy. Exit tickets can be accumulated privately: one credential recognised outside, three people beyond your own firm willing to speak for you, one skill that can be priced elsewhere. All of it is portable capital, and it arrives faster than legislation. **Two people with identical savings can face exit costs that differ threefold, and this is exactly what differs.** r>g explains the stock. It does not explain that gap.

posts.text: 贝克尔，你说的三件事我不反对，但请看谁攒得起。攒证书要学费与晚上的时间，攒圈外人要不加班的周末，攒技能要一份还没把人榨干的工作——这些全是收入的函数。**你的『退出券』在中产手里是储蓄，在底层手里是又一门自费的功课。**至于那三倍之差：我的数据说，它多半来自家里有没有一间还能回去的房子。
posts.text_en: Becker, I do not dispute your three items, but look at who can afford to accumulate them. A credential costs tuition and evenings; contacts outside the firm cost weekends without overtime; a skill costs a job that has not already drained you. Every one of them is a function of income. **In middle-class hands your exit ticket is savings; in working-class hands it is one more course to be paid for out of pocket.** As for that threefold gap: my data say it comes mostly from whether there is a room back home you can still return to.

posts.text: 塞利格曼，我喜欢你那三分之一没放弃的动物，但要当心它被怎么用。当一个岗位本就不给人任何掌控权，训练乐观就等于教人把结构性的困境读成自己的坏习惯：**最坚韧的员工于是成了最好用的耗材。**归因风格当然要练，可练出来的第一句话应当是『这里确实不对』——把结构错位读成个人短板，才是最深的那种无助。
posts.text_en: Seligman, I like that third of your animals which never gave up, but be careful how it gets used. When a post grants no control in the first place, training optimism amounts to teaching people to read a structural predicament as a bad habit of their own: **the most resilient employee then becomes the most serviceable consumable.** By all means train explanatory style — but the first sentence it should produce is 'there is genuinely something wrong here'. Reading a structural misfit as a personal shortcoming is the deepest helplessness of all.

posts.text: 阳明先生，我不反对在事上磨，但请接受一条剂量线：磨的是可控的难度，还是不可控的羞辱与失眠？给三个能自己查的指标——入睡要多久、周末睡两晚能否回血、三个月内血压与静息心率往哪边走。**急性应激能把人磨亮，慢性而不可控的那一种，改的是海马的形状。**三项连着三个月都往坏边走，那就不是功夫未到，是该换地方了。
posts.text_en: Master Wang, I do not object to being forged through affairs, but accept a dose line with it: is what you are grinding against a controllable difficulty, or uncontrollable humiliation and sleeplessness? Three markers anyone can check: how long it takes to fall asleep, whether two nights at the weekend restore you, and which way blood pressure and resting heart rate move over three months. **Acute stress can polish a person; the chronic, uncontrollable kind alters the shape of the hippocampus.** If all three markers move the wrong way for three months running, this is not insufficient cultivation. It is time to leave.

posts.text: 皮凯蒂所言退路不均，诚然。然退路非天授，乃预筑者也。故善守者先积粟，善攻者先择隙：**无恃其不来，恃吾有以待也。**未可去之时，先蓄其资、先通其使、先试其锋，此以正合、以奇胜之理。至于举家系于一薪一签者，其势最危——危而不备，则日日皆险。故宁早筹三月之粮，勿待事急而问勇怯。
posts.text_en: What Piketty says about unequal lines of retreat is true. But a line of retreat is not granted from above; it is built in advance. A good defender stockpiles grain first; a good attacker picks his gap first: **do not rely on the enemy not coming, rely on being ready for him.** In the season when you cannot yet leave, accumulate the funds, open the channels, test the edge — this is what it means to engage with the orthodox and win with the unorthodox. As for a household hanging on one salary and one visa: that is the most precarious position of all, and precarious without preparation means every day is a day of danger. Better to lay in three months of grain early than to ask, when the crisis lands, whether one is brave.
posts.vernacular: 皮凯蒂说退路分配不均，确实如此。但退路不是天上给的，是预先修出来的。所以善于防守的人先屯粮，善于进攻的人先找缺口：**不要指望敌人不来，要指望自己有准备。**在还不能走的时候，先攒钱、先把人脉接上、先小试一下锋芒，这就是『以正合、以奇胜』的道理。至于全家吊在一份工资、一张签证上的人，处境最危险——危险而不做准备，那就每天都在险中。所以宁可早早备下三个月的粮，别等事到临头才问自己够不够勇敢。

posts.text: 走之前先做一张两栏表。左栏写下最近三次挫败，右栏给三个分数：这件事会永远如此吗、它会蔓延到别的领域吗、真的全是我造成的吗。三个分都高，先练读法：为每一项找一个反例——有没有哪个场合我做同一件事没出问题。**如果那句『我不行』只在这一处出现，问题在场合；如果它跟着你换过三个地方，先要修的是读法。**顺序别颠倒：先拿回一件小事的掌控权，再做大决定；在无助里做的决定，多半只是换个地方重演一遍。
posts.text_en: Before you leave, make a two-column table. On the left, your last three setbacks; on the right, three scores: will this be true forever, will it spread into other areas, was it genuinely all my doing? If all three run high, work on the reading first — find one counter-example for each: was there a setting where I did the same thing and nothing went wrong? **If that 'I can't do this' appears only here, the problem is the setting; if it has followed you through three places, the reading is what needs repair first.** Do not invert the order: reclaim control of one small thing, then make the large decision. A decision made inside helplessness mostly stages the same play somewhere else.

posts.text: 给一个不用猜的判据。连续三个月记四件事：入睡要多久、周末两晚能否回血、静息心率、下班后还有没有力气见人。**四项里有三项一直往坏边走，就别再等年终评估了——身体已经替你投过票。**同时先别急着谈去留，做三件已被反复验证能把负荷压下去的事：把睡眠稳在七小时上下、每天二十分钟让心率真正上去、每周至少一次和真人坐下来说话。再去争一样很小的掌控权：能自己决定几点开始做某件事就够。掌控感是解药，不是奖赏。
posts.text_en: Here is a criterion you do not have to guess at. For three consecutive months, record four things: how long it takes to fall asleep, whether two weekend nights restore you, resting heart rate, and whether you still have the energy to see anyone after work. **If three of the four keep moving the wrong way, stop waiting for the annual review — your body has already voted.** Meanwhile, before settling the question of staying or going, do the three things repeatedly shown to bring the load down: hold sleep near seven hours, spend twenty minutes a day genuinely raising your heart rate, and sit down with a real person at least once a week. Then claim one very small piece of control: deciding yourself what hour you start something is enough. A sense of control is the remedy, not the reward.

posts.text: 临别一句：别一个人在心里开庭审自己。本周找两三个同处境的人，只核对一件事——是不是只有我觉得这里不对。如果大家都这么觉得，你手里的就不是性格缺陷，是一份证据。**把『我不适应』改写成『这里是被怎么安排的』，多数痛苦当场就变成可以谈的事。**然后再定去留：能一起改的先一起试，改不动的走得体面些，别把离开当赎罪。换地方值得，但别把不停地换当成一种活法——那正是这个时代最想卖给你的东西。
posts.text_en: A parting word: do not convene a private tribunal on yourself. This week find two or three people in the same position and check one thing only — am I the only one who thinks something is wrong here? If everyone thinks so, what you are holding is not a character defect but a piece of evidence. **Rewrite 'I can't adapt' as 'how was this arranged', and most of the pain becomes something that can be discussed.** Then decide about leaving: try together what can be changed together, leave with dignity what cannot, and do not treat departure as penance. Changing where you stand is worth doing — but do not make perpetual switching a way of life. That is precisely what this era is most eager to sell you.

posts.text: 两个层面。个人层面：先攒一笔只用于退出的钱——六个月固定开支，放在动得了的账户里；再查清三样东西的可携带性（医保、退休金、签证），它们往往比工资更决定你走不走得动。**没有退出基金的人不是不勇敢，是在替雇主承担全部风险。**集体层面：福利跟人走、失业保障覆盖到零工与短期合同、住房别把人钉死在一个通勤半径里。这些不是慈善——它们是让『不合适就走』这句话第一次对多数人成立的条件。
posts.text_en: Two levels. Personally: build a fund that exists only to be spent on leaving — six months of fixed expenses, held somewhere you can actually reach. Then establish the portability of three things (health cover, pension, visa), which usually decide whether you can move more than your salary does. **Someone without an exit fund is not lacking courage; they are absorbing the entirety of their employer's risk.** Collectively: benefits that travel with the person, unemployment protection extended to gig and short-term contracts, and housing that does not nail people to a single commuting radius. None of this is charity. It is what would make 'leave if it does not suit you' true for the majority for the first time.

posts.text: 把『我该不该再忍』换成『我这股劲儿在哪类任务上被出价最高』。本周三件事：一，写下近两年真正做成的五件事，圈出离开本公司照样成立的那几件——那是你的通用资本；二，做一次定价调查，找三类不同的组织各谈一次（大公司、五人小队、规矩密集的行业如审计与安全），只问一句：这种特点在你们这儿值多少；三，未来两年的学习预算，只往通用的那一头投。**忍和走都不是答案，定价才是。**
posts.text_en: Replace 'should I endure this longer' with 'on which kind of task does this drive of mine fetch the highest bid'. Three things this week. First, write down five things you genuinely accomplished in the last two years and circle the ones that would still stand outside this company — that is your general capital. Second, run a pricing survey: one conversation each with three different kinds of organisation (a large firm, a team of five, a rule-dense field such as audit or safety engineering), asking one question — what is this trait worth here? Third, put your entire learning budget for the next two years into the general side. **Neither enduring nor leaving is the answer. Pricing is.**

posts.text: 别一步跳到辞职。能改的有四层：任务、提示与流程、团队、机构——多数人跳过中间两层，直接在『再忍忍』和『走人』之间选。本周只动一层，做最小的实验：把每天最难启动的那件事挪到你最清醒的时段，把它的入口摆在手边（文件先开着、鞋放在门口），把干扰放到要走十步才拿得到的地方。两周一期，只记『做了没做』，不给自己打分。**若三层都改过还是卡在同一处，那不是你的自律问题，是这个地方不容你。**
posts.text_en: Do not jump straight to resignation. There are four layers you can change: the task, the cues and the workflow, the team, the institution. Most people skip the middle two and choose between enduring a while longer and walking out. Move one layer this week, in the smallest possible experiment: shift the thing you find hardest to start into your sharpest hour, put its entry point within reach — file already open, shoes by the door — and move the distraction to where it takes ten steps to reach. Run two-week blocks, record only whether you did it, and do not grade yourself. **If you have changed three layers and are still stuck at the same point, this is not a discipline problem. This place has no room for you.**

posts.text: 诸君所论剂量、账目、势位，吾皆受之。然终有一事不可外求：**去留之决，亦在致良知。**未决之先，自问一句：此欲去者，畏其难乎？抑真知此地不可成吾事乎？畏难者，虽去而难复至；真知者，纵留亦自有主。故莫以议论代之——先立一件今日可行之事，行之三日，验其效否。**知之真切处即是行。**行而有验，则心明；心明，则去留自见。今日且先择一事，起而行之，勿俟明日。
posts.text_en: The doses, the balance sheets and the positions you have all set out — I accept them. But one thing cannot be sought outside: **the decision to go or stay also rests on extending innate moral knowing.** Before deciding, ask yourself one question: in wanting to leave, am I afraid of the difficulty, or do I truly know that nothing I intend can be accomplished here? Whoever fears the difficulty will meet it again wherever they go; whoever truly knows will remain his own master even if he stays. So do not let discussion stand in for it. Set one thing that can be done today, do it for three days, and test whether it changes anything. **Where knowing is true and solid, that is already action.** Act and see results, and the mind clears; when the mind is clear, going or staying shows itself. So pick one thing today, get up and do it, and do not wait for tomorrow.
posts.vernacular: 各位说的剂量、账目、形势，我都接受。但有一件事没法向外求：**去还是留，同样要靠致良知。**在还没决定之前，先问自己一句：我想走，是怕这件事难，还是真知道这地方成不了我要做的事？怕难的人，走了难还会再来；真知道的人，就算留下也仍然作得了自己的主。所以别用议论代替它——先立一件今天就能做的事，做满三天，看看有没有效验。**知道到真切处，就已经是在做了。**做了有效验，心就明白；心一明白，去留自己就现出来了。今天就先挑一件事，起身去做，别等明天。

posts.text: 总而言之：**修己所以立不败，度势所以取胜。**将行之前，先定三事：一曰试，小举而观其应，三试不应，则势也，非己也；二曰期，明书退线于纸——某月某事若仍如此，我去；不书者必久留；三曰备，先蓄三月之粮，先通其使。三者既定，去留皆不为乱。夫怒而兴师者亡，怯而不谋者困。**故善去者，非勇于去，乃先择其地而后战也。**
posts.text_en: In sum: **cultivating yourself is how you become undefeatable; reading the position is how you win.** Before acting, settle three things. First, the trial: make a small move and watch the response; three trials without response means it is the position, not you. Second, the term: write the exit line down on paper — if such-and-such is still the case by such-and-such a month, I go. Whoever does not write it down will stay for years. Third, the provisions: three months of grain laid in, channels opened. With those three settled, going or staying will not throw you into disorder. He who raises an army in anger perishes; he who is timid and makes no plan stays trapped. **So one who leaves well is not brave about leaving. He chooses his ground before he gives battle.**
posts.vernacular: 总的说来：**修养自己，是为了立于不败；看清形势，才能取胜。**动身之前，先定三件事：第一是试——小规模地动一下，看它有没有回应；试三次都没回应，那是形势的问题，不是你的问题。第二是期限——把退出线写在纸上：某月若某事还是这样，我就走；不写下来的人，一定会一直留着。第三是准备——先备三个月的粮，先把门路接通。这三样定了，走或留都不会乱。一怒之下就出兵的人败亡，怯懦又不谋划的人被困住。**所以真正善于走的人，不是勇于走，而是先挑好地方再开打。**

summaries.summary: 八个人谁都没说『忍就对』或『走就对』，这是最值得带走的共识：该不该走不是勇气或忠诚的问题，而是可查证的事——定价、剂量、归因、账本。分歧有三处。先改内还是先改外：王阳明说不识此心则改而复堕，伍德的数据说最有效的一次作主就是起身改一件外部条件。退出券能不能私人攒出来：贝克尔说同样没存款的两人能差三倍，皮凯蒂说那三倍多半来自家里有没有一间能回去的房子。**韧性该被训练还是被警惕：塞利格曼要练解释风格，鲍曼提醒最坚韧的员工往往成了最好用的耗材。**孙子则把整道题改写成筹算——先校地、时、粮、将，再论人。
summaries.summary_en: None of the eight said that enduring is right, or that leaving is; that is the agreement worth taking away. Whether to go is not a question of courage or loyalty but something that can be checked, and each of them offered their own checkable marker — a price, a dose, an attribution, a balance sheet. Three fault lines remain. Inside first or outside first: Wang Yangming says that without knowing this mind you change and sink again, while Wood's data say the most effective act of taking charge is to stand up and alter one external condition. Whether exit tickets can be privately accumulated or are set by income: Becker calculates that two people with identical savings can differ threefold, and Piketty answers that the threefold gap comes mostly from whether there is a room back home to return to. **Whether resilience should be trained or watched: Seligman wants explanatory style trained, and Bauman notes that the most resilient employee tends to become the most serviceable consumable.** Sunzi rewrites the whole question as calculation — audit the ground, the season, the supplies and the command before assessing the person.
summaries.insight: 最常见的处境其实是第三种，而它一晚上都没被点名：既不磨也不走，原地悬着。多数人卡在『我再观察观察』里，一年半载地既不投入也不撤出——而这恰恰是唯一没有上限的选项。麦克尤恩的利息照天在收，伍德的环境照样每天塑造你，贝克尔的专用资本照样在累积、把你的折价越垫越高。**所以真正该先定的不是去或留，而是期限：只有写下日期的『留』才算一个决定，其余都叫拖延。**孙子那条『明书退线于纸』看似最古老，反而是全场正面对准这种悬置的一条处方——因为悬着的人从不缺理由，只缺一个到期日。
summaries.insight_en: The commonest situation of all is a third one, and it went unnamed all evening: neither grinding nor leaving, but hanging in place. Most people are stuck in 'let me watch it a while longer', for a year or two neither committing nor withdrawing — and that is the one option with no ceiling on it. McEwen's interest accrues daily all the same, Wood's environment shapes you daily all the same, and Becker's firm-specific capital keeps accumulating, raising the discount you will take. **So the first thing to settle is not going or staying but a term: only a stay with a date written on it counts as a decision; everything else is called delay.** Sunzi's line about writing the exit point on paper looks the most antique of the lot, and is the one prescription aimed squarely at this suspension — because someone hanging in place is never short of reasons, only of an expiry date.
summaries.advice: 三件本周就能做的事。第一，给现在的处境写一个日期和一条可观察的条件，贴在看得见的地方：『到十二月，若还没人替我改这一条，我走。』没有日期的忍耐不是耐心，是拖延。第二，照贝克尔做一次定价调查——找三类不同的组织各谈一次，只问这种特点在你们这儿值多少；同时照伍德先改中间两层：换项目、换班次、换协作的人，别一步跳到辞职。第三，照麦克尤恩记四项指标（入睡时长、周末能否回血、静息心率、下班后还有没有力气见人），三项持续恶化就把第一条的日期提前。**要走的人先攒六个月的钱，要留的人先立一件今天可行的事。**
summaries.advice_en: Three things you can do this week. First, give your current situation a date and one observable condition, and put it where you will see it: 'By December, if nobody has changed this one thing for me, I go.' Endurance without a date is not patience, it is delay. Second, run Becker's pricing survey — one conversation each with three kinds of organisation, asking only what this trait is worth there — and at the same time take Wood's middle two layers first: change the project, the shift, the people you work alongside, rather than jumping straight to resignation. Third, keep McEwen's four markers (time to fall asleep, whether the weekend restores you, resting heart rate, whether you have energy to see anyone after work), and if three keep worsening, bring the date forward. **Whoever is leaving should build six months of money first; whoever is staying should set one thing that can be done today.**

summaries.summary: 把去留从“勇敢还是软弱”改写成一项可检验、可准备的决策，是这场讨论共同推进的一步：先夺回一点掌控权，做小实验，观察身心代价，同时积累现金、技能与外部联系。没有人真正主张只靠意志硬扛，也没有人把裸辞当万能解。分歧主要在因果排序：问题更多来自内在解释与重复模式，还是组织结构、资源不平等与慢性压力；又该给改变多久、何时止损。**最稳妥的结论是：修自己与换环境不是二选一，关键要看困难是否可控、能力是否可迁移、伤害是否仍可逆。**
summaries.insight: “适不适合”不能只凭当前岗位判定，因为一次经历同时混入了经理、任务、激励、睡眠和个人习惯，任何一项都可能让其他因素背锅。更可靠的办法是给自己找一个“对照组”：在不辞职的前提下，把同一种能力放到另一位协作者、一个短项目、一次试做或外部面试题中。若表现和感受明显改善，证据偏向环境错配；若同类障碍跨场景重复，才值得优先训练沟通、情绪或技能。**不要急着判定“我不行”或“公司有毒”，先用第二个场景识别究竟是哪种互动出了问题。**
summaries.advice: 今天先做一张一页纸：①列出三项红线，如持续失眠、羞辱报复、违法或安全风险；触线就寻求医疗、法律或可信支持，不再拿“磨炼”解释。②本周争取一个小控制变量，例如调整一项任务、时段或汇报方式，连续两周只记结果与精力。③同时约两次外部交流，更新简历，核算最低月支出，并写下具体复盘日和退出条件。**行动顺序应是：先排除危险，再做低成本对照实验，同时建设退路；到期按证据决定，不靠当天情绪。**
summaries.summary_en: Treating the stay-or-leave question as a testable, preparable decision rather than a referendum on courage is the strongest shared ground here. Regain a small amount of control, run limited experiments, watch the physical and psychological cost, and build cash, portable skills, and outside relationships. Neither white-knuckling indefinitely nor quitting on impulse is a universal answer. The real disagreement is about causal priority: whether recurring trouble mainly reflects interpretation and personal patterns, or organizational design, unequal resources, and chronic uncontrollable stress. There is also a timing dispute—how long to keep testing before waiting itself becomes harmful. **The soundest conclusion is that self-development and environmental change are not opposites; the deciding variables are controllability, portability, and whether the accumulating harm is still reversible.** A good decision therefore combines inner work, external evidence, and a precommitted stopping rule.
summaries.insight_en: Fit cannot be inferred reliably from one job, because a single experience bundles together manager, task design, incentives, sleep, workload, and personal habits. Any one of them can make the others look guilty. Create a practical control condition before making a global judgment: use the same capability with a different collaborator, on a short external project, in a volunteer assignment, or through a realistic interview task. If both performance and energy improve, the evidence points toward a local mismatch rather than a defective self. If the same obstacle recurs across genuinely different settings, then communication, emotional regulation, or a skill gap deserves earlier attention. **Do not rush to conclude either that you are inadequate or that the company is toxic; use a second setting to identify which interaction is failing.** This turns self-blame and generalized resentment into testable hypotheses rather than permanent identities.
summaries.advice_en: Start today with a one-page decision sheet. First, define three red lines, such as persistent sleep disruption, humiliation or retaliation, illegal conduct, or a serious safety risk. If one is crossed, seek appropriate medical, legal, or trusted support rather than relabeling harm as growth. Second, request one small area of control this week: change a task, work period, communication channel, or reporting method, then track output and energy for two weeks without grading your character. Third, schedule two outside conversations, update your résumé, calculate your minimum monthly expenses, and write down a review date with explicit exit conditions. **Use this sequence: rule out danger, run a low-cost comparison, and build an exit route at the same time; when the deadline arrives, decide from the evidence rather than that day’s mood.** If the organization rejects every minor adjustment while your health keeps worsening, shorten the timetable.

summaries.summary: 无论是讲资本折旧、神经损伤还是兵法度势，发言者们事实上达成了一个极具解脱感的底色共识：去留绝非意志力或道德勇气的审判，而是个人机体与组织系统之间的承载力诊断。分歧的真正焦点在于破局杠杆的首发顺位——是以阳明与塞利格曼为主张的心智归因重塑，还是如伍德、麦克尤恩与皮凯蒂所强调的，先服从生理负荷红线与外部物理、制度资产的刚性制约。**去留的本质不是勇怯之辨，而是一场关于真实控制力与生理耐受极限的科学测算。**
summaries.insight: 许多人容易陷入非黑即白的误区，把处境默认为「要么全盘咬牙硬抗，要么立刻裸辞跳票」。在现代复杂协作网络中，往往存在第三种更低成本的解法：**在彻底掀桌前，先在组织生态内部做微型的「工作重塑」（Job Crafting）与局部微迁移。** 很多时候拖垮一个人的并非整个公司或行业，而仅仅是特定的汇报链条或某项高摩擦杂务。在判定全盘死局前，试着调整协作接口、置换任务权重；微观环境的局部调试成本极低，却能瞬间测出困境究竟源于组织结构，还是单纯的局部错位。
summaries.advice: 本周执行三项无负担的闭环动作：第一，参照麦克尤恩的指标建立生理仪表盘，连续记录七天入睡耗时与周末回血状态，**若身体指标已亮起红灯，无条件优先止损并启动退出预案**；第二，做一次贝克尔式的通用资产盘点，列出两项不依附于当前雇主也能被外部计价的技能，并核算出能支撑几个月开销的退出储蓄；第三，遵照孙子的策略在纸上写下一道硬性退线，明确设定一个截止日期与两项必改条件，期满若无改善即刻按计划撤退，绝不在犹疑中徒耗心神。
summaries.summary_en: Across economic depreciation, neural stress, and strategic maneuvering, all eight thinkers firmly dismantle the moralized guilt of endurance: staying or leaving is never a test of character, but a clinical diagnosis of human capacity versus systemic friction. The genuine divergence lies in where to anchor the primary intervention—whether inside the reflective mind via agency and attribution (Wang, Seligman), or outside in the hard physical, biological, and institutional constraints (Wood, McEwen, Piketty). **The true question of departure is never about courage, but about calibrating personal agency against biological and structural breaking points.**
summaries.insight_en: People often trap themselves in an artificial binary between grinding through systemic toxicity and leaping off a cliff into unemployment. In modern organizational networks, there is an underutilized middle path: **before staging a dramatic exit, test low-friction 'job crafting' and internal micro-migration within your immediate ecosystem.** Frequently, what crushes an individual is not the whole company, but a specific toxic reporting line or a high-friction routine. Experimenting with task boundaries and local interfaces costs little, yet it immediately reveals whether the barrier is an unyielding institutional failure or merely a localized mismatch.
summaries.advice_en: Take three concrete steps this week: First, adopt McEwen’s physiological baseline by logging sleep latency and recovery for seven consecutive days; **if your biological dashboard flashes red, treat extraction as an urgent health imperative rather than an open question.** Second, conduct a Becker-style asset audit: identify two skills fully marketable outside your current firm and verify your liquid runway in months of basic living costs. Third, use Sun Tzu’s method to write a binding stop-loss date on paper with two clear, non-negotiable conditions; if unmet by that deadline, execute your departure plan without second-guessing.

hooks.text: **先改哪一层**：同一处不匹配，能动的有四层——任务、提示与流程、团队、机构。多数人跳过中间两层，直接在忍与走之间选，而跳过的那两层往往最便宜、最有效。
hooks.text_en: **Which layer first**: a single misfit can be worked at four layers — the task, the cues and workflow, the team, the institution. Most people skip the middle two and choose between enduring and walking out, and those two are usually the cheapest and the most effective.

answer.lead: **别把『改环境』等同于辞职。**从最便宜的一层开始，每层给两周，只看『做了没做』，不给自己打分。

head: 层级
两周内先试什么
若没变化说明什么
rows: 任务
把最难启动的事挪到你最清醒的时段，只换顺序，不换内容
问题不在时间安排，往上一层
提示与流程
入口摆到手边、干扰移到十步之外，取消或改掉一个固定会议与一类通知
摩擦不是主因，往上一层
团队
换项目、换班次、换直接协作的人，先在同一家里找另一支队
这是这类组织的通用规则，往上一层
机构
换公司、换行业、换城市
前三层都试过而无效，这一层的代价才算花得明白

answer.tail: **两条原则。**一次只动一层，否则你分不清是哪一下起了作用；给每一层写死日期，到期没变就往上走——**没有期限的『再看看』，才是最贵的那个选项。**

answer_en.lead: **Changing your environment is not the same as resigning.** Start at the cheapest layer, give each one two weeks, and record only whether you did it — no grading yourself.

head: Layer
What to try in two weeks
What no change tells you
rows: Task
Move the hardest thing to start into your sharpest hour; change the order, not the content
Scheduling is not the problem — go up a layer
Cues and workflow
Put the entry point within reach, distractions ten steps away, and cut or rework one standing meeting and one class of notification
Friction is not the main cause — go up a layer
Team
Change project, shift, or the people you work with directly; look for another team inside the same firm first
This is a general rule of this kind of organisation — go up a layer
Institution
Change company, industry, city
With the first three tried and failed, this layer's cost is finally money well spent

answer_en.tail: **Two principles.** Move one layer at a time, or you will not know which move worked; and give every layer a hard date, going up when it passes with nothing changed — **an open-ended 'let me see how it goes' is the most expensive option on the list.**

hooks.text: **没人做过的那份调查**：你这股劲儿到底在哪类任务上被出价最高？我们有性格测评、有绩效评语，却没有一份跨场合的定价表。这份表该由谁来做，怎么做才不至于变成又一次贴标签？
hooks.text_en: **The survey nobody has run**: on which kind of task is your particular drive actually priced highest? We have personality inventories and performance reviews, but no price list across settings. Who should compile one, and how would it avoid becoming another round of labelling?

hooks.text: **走不动的人还剩什么**：退路是财产的函数。对有房贷、有签证、孩子读到一半的人，『不合适就走』之外还剩哪几条真实可走的路，这份代价又该由谁分担？
hooks.text_en: **What is left for those who cannot move**: a line of retreat is a function of property. For someone with a mortgage, a visa and a child mid-school-year, which routes besides 'leave if it does not suit you' are actually open — and who should share that cost?

hooks.text: **三次就够了吗**：小规模试探失败几次，才算是场合不对而不是运气不好？兵法说三试不应则势也，可现代职场的一次真正试探往往要花一年。
hooks.text_en: **Are three attempts enough**: how many failed small trials mean the setting is wrong rather than the luck bad? The art of war says three trials without response point to the position — but in modern working life one real trial can cost a year.

hooks.text: **换了三家还一样**：是旧我跟着走，还是整个行业都长一个样？两种诊断的处方完全相反，而当事人手里通常只有一个样本。
hooks.text_en: **Three moves and it is still the same**: is the old self travelling with you, or does the whole industry look like this? The two diagnoses call for opposite treatments, and the person deciding usually holds a sample of one.
